name: heralded-memory
question: Which experiments have demonstrated heralded entanglement between two remote quantum memories, and what herald rate, Bell-state fidelity and storage time did each report?

Q0.label: main
Q0.text: Which experiments have demonstrated heralded entanglement between two remote quantum memories, and what herald rate, Bell-state fidelity and storage time did each report?
Q0.keywords: heralded entanglement remote quantum memories experiment demonstration rate Bell state fidelity storage time

Q1.label: subject
Q1.text: Two spatially separated quantum memory nodes, such as trapped ions, neutral atoms in cavities, nitrogen-vacancy or silicon-vacancy centres in diamond, rare-earth doped crystals or cold atomic ensembles, connected by optical photons.
Q1.keywords: quantum memory nodes trapped ion neutral atom cavity NV centre SiV diamond rare-earth crystal atomic ensemble spin photon interface

Q2.label: approach
Q2.text: Heralded entanglement generation in which photons emitted by each memory interfere at a midpoint station and a detector click heralds success, using single-photon or two-photon Barrett-Kok schemes and a photonic Bell-state measurement.
Q2.keywords: heralded entanglement generation two-photon interference Bell-state measurement single-photon scheme Barrett-Kok midpoint station detector click entanglement swapping

Q3.label: outcome
Q3.text: Reported performance of remote entanglement: heralding or entanglement generation rate per second or per attempt, fidelity of the heralded state to a target Bell state, and memory coherence or storage time of the entangled qubits.
Q3.keywords: entanglement generation rate success probability per attempt heralding rate Bell state fidelity coherence time storage time memory lifetime T2

Q4.label: context
Q4.text: Memory nodes located in separate laboratories or buildings and linked by optical fiber, sometimes with frequency conversion to telecom wavelengths, over distances from metres to tens of kilometres in a metropolitan network.
Q4.keywords: separate laboratories buildings optical fiber link telecom wavelength frequency conversion kilometres metropolitan deployed fiber quantum network
